newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Money demand rose in May in central Franc Zone.
newsitem.headline: Money demand rose in May in central Franc Zone.

text.p: Demand for central bank funds in the Central African part of the Franc Zone rose in May for the fifth consecutive month, due largely to commodity marketing season demand in Chad, the monthly central bank bulletin said.

The Bank of Central African States (BEAC) said the average daily volume of funds allocated to eligible credit institutions rose by 5.8 percent to 40.4 billion CFA francs ($69 million) in May from 38.2 billion in April.
The BEAC is the central bank for Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Gabon and Equatorial Guinea.

Banks in Chad, busy financing the cotton marketing season, drew down 29.5 billion CFA francs daily in May from the bank's main short-term lending window (Guichet A), which accounted for the majority of loans from that source.
Total Guichet A loans came to 34.1 billion CFA francs daily, on average.
Central bank lending from Guichet B, which offers medium term credits, also increased in May to 608 million CFA francs from 517 million in April.

Interbank market activity continued to pick up after a sharp decrease in March, when it fell to 1.3 billion CFA francs from 6.3 billion in February. Total transactions registered 2.4 billion in May after 1.9 billion in April.
The average interbank rate rose in May to 5.723 percent, from 5.263 percent in April, reflecting the rise in demand.
The BEAC drained more money from the banking system in May, but it stressed that the liquidity system varied greatly between countries in the region.
It drew 87.3 billion CFA francs from the system through money market tenders, up from 84.2 billion in April and 82.7 billion CFA in March.
"The increase in surplus bank reserves is mainly due to the early repayment of loans granted to oil companies and to the repatriation of export receipts " said the bulletin.
Banks in Cameroon offered the highest average daily amount, 43.3 billion CFA francs, against 38.4 billion CFA in April.
Gabonese bank offers dipped slightly in May to 32.7 billion CFA francs against 35.4 billion in April due to increased demand for construction loans by small- and medium-sized companies.
Official BEAC rates were cut with effect from May 23.

The intervention rate fell to 7.50 percent from 7.75 percent and the two-to-seven-day lending rate to 9.50 percent from 9.75 percent. ($1=580 CFA francs) -- Clare Black, Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
